post.caption: Gems were polished smooth before faceting. A cabochon has a smooth domed top and a flat back. Until the late Middle Ages, gems were simply cut this way, and the V&A says most medieval ring gems are cabochons. Faceting began to spread around the 1400s. Early diamond cuts just polished the crystal's natural faces. A diamond dust wheel, the scaif, arrived in the late 1400s. Star sapphires and cat's-eyes are still cut this way, because facets would hide the star or the eye. Turquoise is most often cut into cabochons.
